init.summary: Create local Blocks workspace files: blocks.json, data schema/rules folders, and .env.example.

doctor.summary: Inspect cached CLI version, Node.js, OIDC config, token, optional project, and storage health.
doctor.details: Account-only mode is valid. Performs no token refresh, network request, or state write. The 'CLI up to date' check reads the daily-cached npm registry lookup; an outdated version is reported (JSON: cliUpdateAvailable) but never fails the run -- ask the user before running 'npm install -g @seliseblocks/cli-os@latest'.

login.details: Prints a verification URL and user code, opens the browser to the verification page when possible so you only need to click approve, then polls until the device is authorized; bootstraps a missing named profile without importing credentials, stores account access and refresh tokens, and makes that account active. If a project was previously selected, re-impersonates it automatically; otherwise lists projects and prompts you to run 'blocks use <tenantId>'.

auth status.summary: Show only whether account/project access and refresh tokens are missing, valid, expired, or available.
auth status.details: Does not print account config values.

auth refresh.summary: Force account token refresh, or project token refresh with --project.

auth remove.summary: Clear cached tokens and stored local credentials for that account.
auth remove.details: The packaged default OS account is restored from package defaults.

logout.summary: Revoke the current refresh token when possible and remove local session data.

projects create.summary: Create a new Blocks project via /os/v4/Project/Create using the account token (no project needs to be selected yet).
projects create.details: Creates exactly one application, always in the 'dev' environment -- environment, domain, cookie domain, and production flag are fixed and not configurable here; the domain sent is a placeholder the platform discards and replaces with the one it assigns. Confirms first because it accepts the Blocks terms on your behalf. Refuses a name already used by another project unless --allow-duplicate-name is passed. Verifies the result against Project/Gets and prints the new tenantId, tenantGroupId, and assigned domain. Does not select the project -- run 'blocks use <tenantId>' next. If the account is in project mode, temporarily stops that session for the account-level create call and restores it afterward.

projects list.details: Uses the impersonated project session when a project is selected, otherwise the account token. Read-only.

projects get.details: Uses selected project when tenantId is omitted. Pass --deployment to also include the environment, tenantGroupId, and linked repo assets (from Project/GetAsset) that 'release deploy' uses to resolve its target. Read-only.

use.summary: Save the selected project tenant for the resolved account and in blocks.json, then immediately impersonate it.
use.details: If a different project was selected, stops that impersonation first to reclaim a fresh account refresh token before starting the new one.

deselect.summary: Stop the active impersonation (restoring a fresh account refresh token), then clear that account's selected project tenant and blocks.json entry...
deselect.details: Stop the active impersonation (restoring a fresh account refresh token), then clear that account's selected project tenant and blocks.json entry and drop its cached impersonation token. Run 'blocks use <tenantId>' again to reselect and re-impersonate.

iam me.summary: Read the current user from IAM (bootstrapping/CLI operator identity, not a project resource).
iam me.details: The server resolves this to the root identity either way, so the impersonated project session works too.

iam users list.summary: Query users with paging, sorting, and filters.
iam users list.details: Convenience filters are --email/--name/--organization-id. For any other filter, pass a raw JSON object in --body/--file with a "filter" key, e.g. --body '{"filter":{"isActive":true}}'; the convenience flags are merged over it.

iam users get.summary: Read one IAM user by id.

iam users create.details: Requires --email or --user-name; omit --password to let the user set their own via activation mail.

iam users update.summary: Update an existing IAM user's profile fields, roles, or permissions.

iam users activate.summary: Enable a disabled IAM user account.
iam users activate.details: Not the same as the user completing their own activation link.

iam users deactivate.summary: Disable an IAM user account, suspending their access.

iam users access grant.summary: Grant roles or permissions to an IAM user.

iam users access revoke.summary: Revoke an IAM user's roles and permissions.

iam users exists.summary: Check whether an IAM user with this email exists.

iam email available.summary: Check whether an email address is free to register.

iam roles list.summary: List IAM roles defined in the project.

iam roles get.summary: Read one IAM role by id.

iam roles create.details: Role hierarchy keys off --parent-role-slug, not itemId.

iam roles update.summary: Update an IAM role's name, description, or parent.

iam roles assign-permissions.summary: Add or remove permissions on a role, addressed by slug.
iam roles assign-permissions.details: Resolves permission resource strings to itemIds first.

iam roles assignable.summary: List the roles the current caller is allowed to assign to others.

iam permissions list.details: --type is ResourceType (0-3), --severity is PermissionSeverity (0 None, 1 Critical .. 4 Low).

iam permissions get.summary: Read one IAM permission by id.

iam permissions update.summary: Update an IAM permission definition, including archiving it.

iam permissions by-severity.summary: List permissions filtered by severity and resource type.
iam permissions by-severity.details: --severity is PermissionSeverity, ordered most-severe-first, not least: 0 None, 1 Critical, 2 High, 3 Medium, 4 Low. --type is IAM's ResourceType: 0 None, 1 Endpoint, 2 FrontendAction, 3 DataProtection.

iam resources features.summary: List IAM feature flags for the active user context.

iam organizations update.summary: Update an organization's profile and locale settings.

iam organizations my.summary: List the signed-in user's own organizations.

iam organizations config get.summary: Read the tenant's organization policy, including isMultiOrgEnabled.

iam organizations config save.details: Boolean flags only turn settings on; use --body to switch one off.

iam signup-settings save.details: Boolean flags only turn settings on; use --body to switch one off.

mfa totp setup.summary: Start TOTP enrollment for the impersonated user.

mfa totp enable.summary: Composed enrollment: totp setup -> (scan the printed QR/secret, enter the code -- interactively prompted if --code is omitted) -> totp...
mfa totp enable.details: Composed enrollment: totp setup -> (scan the printed QR/secret, enter the code -- interactively prompted if --code is omitted) -> totp verify-setup -> method set --mfa-type <n> -> backup-codes generate. One sitting, one confirmation. Non-interactive callers must pass --code or receive interactive_input_required. --mfa-type is required and not defaulted: pass IAM UserMfaType 1 for TOTP (the same value plain mfa method set expects).

mfa generate.summary: Send an OTP challenge; returns an mfaId to pass to resend/verify.

mfa resend.summary: Re-send a pending OTP challenge for an existing mfaId.

mfa verify.summary: Verify an OTP or step-up challenge.
mfa verify.details: --auth-type is the UserMfaType that issued it.

mfa method set.summary: Switch the impersonated user's active MFA method.
mfa method set.details: IAM only branches on 1 (TOTP) and 2 (Email) here -- any other value falls through to its disable path and turns the user's MFA off. Use 'blocks mfa disable' when that is what you mean.

mfa disable.summary: Disable MFA for the impersonated user.

mfa backup-codes list.summary: Returns { remaining: <count> } only -- the codes themselves are shown once, at generate.

mfa backup-codes generate.summary: Mint a fresh set of MFA backup codes, invalidating existing ones.

mfa backup-codes use.details: Anonymous endpoint, hence the explicit userId.

mail config list.summary: List SMTP/inbound mail configurations for the selected project.

mail config get.summary: Read one mail configuration by name.

mail config save.summary: Create or update an SMTP / inbound mail server configuration.
mail config save.details: Upsert: omit --configuration-id to create; pass it to update. --provider and --port are raw integers. --account-password is redacted from dry-run output, but the live response and the stored value are still sensitive.

mail config duplicate.summary: Copy an existing mail configuration into a new one.

mail template list.summary: List mail templates, optionally filtered by configuration.

mail template get.summary: Read one mail template by itemId.

mail template save.summary: Create or update a mail template for one language.
mail template save.details: Upsert: omit --item-id to create; pass it to update.

mail template clone.summary: Copy a mail template into a new one.

mail mailbox list.details: Filters are date, status, search and direction only; there is no --configuration-id.

mail mailbox get.summary: Read one mailbox message by id.

mail send.summary: Send an email through the tenant's default mail configuration (/logic/v4/Mail/Send).

mail sendtoany.summary: Same as mail send but via /logic/v4/Mail/SendToAny, which lets the mail provider route the send (e.g.

notification save.summary: Pass --update when saving over an existing notification configuration.

notifier notify.summary: Push a notification to specific users/roles, or everyone matching a subscription filter.
notifier notify.details: Target with at least one of --user-ids/--roles/--subscription-filters.

notifier unread.summary: Read unread notifications matching a subscription filter.
notifier unread.details: Sent as query parameters even though swagger documents this endpoint as GET with a JSON body -- the Fetch spec forbids a body on GET. Read-only.

notifier mark-all-read.summary: Mark every notification as read for the caller.

storage config get.summary: Read one storage backend configuration by name.

storage config save.summary: Upsert: omit --item-id to create; pass --update to update.

auth idp get.summary: Read one identity provider by id.

auth idp create.summary: Register an identity provider so end users can sign in through it.
auth idp create.details: Apple-specific fields (teamId, keyId, privateKey, appleAudience) go in --body/--file so no private key lands in shell history. IAM's create endpoint stores issuer/jwksUri/wellKnownUrl but drops authorizationUrl/tokenUrl/userInfoUrl -- set those with 'auth idp update' afterward.

auth idp update.summary: provider/providerType/protocol/clientId are immutable: omit them, or echo the existing values exactly if you also pass --body/--file.
auth idp update.details: The only endpoint that persists authorizationUrl/tokenUrl/userInfoUrl -- create accepts and drops them, and update never re-runs discovery, so values set here stick. Use it to repair a provider whose authorizationUrl came back null: '/idp/initiate' builds its redirect from that field, so hosted login goes nowhere without it. Read the endpoint values from the tenant's discovery document rather than composing them by hand.

auth idp delete.summary: Irreversible; also deletes the related OIDC client registration.

auth idp status.summary: Enable/disable a provider without deleting its configuration.

auth config get.summary: Read the tenant's AuthController configuration, including isOidcEnabled.

auth config save.details: Fetches and merges current values first. Enabling OIDC requires accountActionBaseUrl.

auth client-credentials list.summary: List this project's machine-to-machine client credentials.
auth client-credentials list.details: clientSecret is included in list responses; treat CLI output as sensitive.

auth client-credentials save.summary: Omit --item-id to create; pass it to update.
auth client-credentials save.details: The response carries no clientSecret; read it back from 'auth client-credentials list', which returns it in full.

auth oidc-clients list.summary: List registered OAuth 2.0 / OIDC client applications for the tenant.
auth oidc-clients list.details: client_secret is NOT excluded by the service -- the CLI redacts it in list/get output. Use rotate-secret to obtain a working secret.

auth oidc-clients save.summary: Upsert: omit --item-id to register a new client, pass it to update an existing one.
auth oidc-clients save.details: The response's client_secret is shown here; the service also returns it on list/get, where the CLI redacts it. --client-type is not optional in practice: IAM derives tokenEndpointAuthMethod from it, so omitting it stores a browser/SPA client as confidential ("client_secret_post") and lets it request the client_credentials grant. Pass --client-type public for any PKCE/browser client. --register-as-identity-provider creates the linked identity provider in the same call. Its authorize/token/userinfo/jwks/issuer values are filled from the discovery document. When omitted, --external-discovery-endpoint defaults to external provider or non-standard IAM base URL.

auth oidc-clients delete.summary: Irreversible; revokes all tokens issued to the client.

auth oidc-clients rotate-secret.summary: Generates a new client_secret, shown once; the old secret stops working immediately.

data validate.summary: Validate local blocks/data/schemas/*.json and blocks/data/rules.json before pushing.

data schema list.summary: List project schemas via /data/v4/schemas using an impersonated project token.
data schema list.details: Read-only. Page defaults are 1/100; fails clearly on an unexpected response shape instead of treating it as an empty list.

data schema pull.summary: Download every project schema (paging through all of them) into blocks/data/schemas/*.json.
data schema pull.details: Strips the API id, project identifiers, and platform-managed fields so the file is portable and re-pushable as-is. Writes local files only.

data schema push.summary: Create or update project schemas via /data/v4/schemas/define.
data schema push.details: Mutating. Looks up the destination project's schema by name -- never trusts a local id/itemId, which may belong to another project -- and uses PUT with the destination id when found, POST otherwise. Warns when a local id is ignored; fails clearly instead of treating an empty response as success.

data rules pull.summary: Download data-access policies into blocks/data/rules.json in the CLI's portable format (schemaName, no itemId/schemaId).

data rules deploy.summary: Apply schema security and data-access policies.
data rules deploy.details: Mutating; supports dry-run and confirmation. Resolves each policy's destination schema id and any existing policy id by name -- never reuses a source-project id.

data reload.summary: Reload Data schema configuration so staged schema/rule changes become live.

data sync.summary: Composed flow: validate local schemas/rules, then data schema push -> data rules deploy -> data reload, so pushed changes actually go live in one...
data sync.details: Composed flow: validate local schemas/rules, then data schema push -> data rules deploy -> data reload, so pushed changes actually go live in one step. Validation runs first and hard-fails before anything is sent if it finds errors. Prints 3 separate step outputs (one per underlying command), not one combined document. One confirmation covers the whole flow.

data config create.summary: Point the Data Gateway at an external database.

data schema get.summary: Non-JSON output also prints the schema's exact GraphQL operation names -- generated names are naive string concatenation, not English...
data schema get.details: Non-JSON output also prints the schema's exact GraphQL operation names -- generated names are naive string concatenation, not English pluralization (e.g. Company -> getCompanys/Companys, not Companies).

data schema get-by-name.summary: Full field-level detail by collection name (info-by-name).

data schema aggregation.summary: Schemas plus an access-level summary (Public/User/Custom x Read/Write/Edit/Delete).

data schema change-logs.summary: Unadapted schema change logs; data reload clears these.

data schema info list.summary: Entity-type schema collections with basic info.

data schema info save.summary: Create schema metadata only (no fields yet) - pair with data schema fields.

data schema info update.summary: Update schema metadata without touching field definitions.

data schema fields.summary: Add/update field definitions; the 'fields' array (name/type/isArray/isPIIData/ isUniqueData/description) goes in --body/--file, e.g.

data rules policy get.summary: Read all data-access policies for one schema.

data rules policy delete.summary: Delete one data-access policy without a full rules pull and deploy.

data validation get.summary: Read one validation rule by id.

data validation by-schema.summary: List validation rules for one schema.

data validation by-schema-field.summary: List validation rules for one field of one schema.

data validation save.summary: Create or update the field-level validation rules on a schema field.
data validation save.details: Upsert: omit --item-id to create, pass it to update. --body must include a "validations" array, e.g. '{"validations":[{"type":1,"value":"^[0-9]+$","isActive":true}]}'.

data files get.summary: Download a file from the storage object tree.

data files get-many.summary: Download several files by id in one call.

data files info.summary: List file metadata records with paging and sorting.

data files upload.summary: Cloud: create file/version metadata, then PUT bytes to the returned URL.
data files upload.details: Local: one multipart request. The file appears in the object tree without registration.

data files presigned-upload-url.summary: Mutating cloud step 1: creates metadata/version and returns uploadUrl/fileId.

data files upload-to-url.summary: PUT a local file straight to a pre-signed storage URL (upload step 2).
data files upload-to-url.details: Follows 'data files presigned-upload-url'. Provider-direct PUT - no x-blocks-key and no bearer token, by design. Adds 'x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob' for Azure; pass --blob-type to change it or --no-blob-type-header to omit it for other providers. The URL's query string is itself a write credential, so dry-run output shows the origin and path only.

data files upload-to-local-storage.summary: One-call alternative to the two commands above, for local-storage-backed projects.

data files delete.summary: Defaults to moving the file to trash; --permanent removes bytes and metadata.

data files list.summary: List object-tree entries under a directory, with cursor paging.

data files search.summary: Search the object tree by name.

data files shared.summary: List object-tree entries shared with the caller.

data files directory-create.summary: Create a directory in the object tree.

data files directory-move.summary: Move a directory under a different parent.

data files create-version.summary: Add a new version to an existing file.

data files copy.summary: Copy a file into another directory.

data files move.summary: Move a file into another directory.

data files access-list.summary: List the access policies attached to a resource.

data files access-resolve.summary: Resolve the effective access a principal has on a resource, including inherited policies.

data files access-grant.summary: Grant a principal access to a file or directory.
data files access-grant.details: --principal-type is one of User, Role, Everyone, or Organization.

data files access-update.summary: Update one access policy on a resource.

data files access-revoke.summary: Remove one access policy from a resource.

data files inheritance.summary: Turn access-policy inheritance on or off for a resource.

data files share.summary: Share a resource with a principal.

localization validate.summary: Validate a local i18n JSON dictionary.
localization validate.details: Supports nested JSON input and validates the flattened key/value set locally.

localization push.summary: Create or update Localization keys from a local i18n JSON dictionary via /localization/v4/Key/SaveKeys.
localization push.details: Creates the module first when it is missing.

localization pull.summary: Download published cloud localization via /localization/v4/Key/GetCloudUilmFile and write a local JSON dictionary.

localization assistant translation-sugge.summary: Ask the localization assistant to suggest a translation for one string.
localization assistant translation-sugge.details: --source-text is required. --glossary-ids constrains the suggestion to agreed terminology; --temperature and --max-character-length tune the output.

localization config get-webhook.summary: Read the tenant's localization change webhook.

localization config save-webhook.summary: Create or update the webhook the Localization service calls on changes.
localization config save-webhook.details: Upsert: omit --item-id to create, pass it to update. --secret and --header-key sign the callback so the receiver can verify it; both are redacted from dry-run output.

localization glossary save.summary: Create or update a glossary term.

localization glossary suggested.summary: Get AI-suggested glossary terms for an entry.

localization key save.summary: Create or update one localization key.

localization key list.summary: Search localization keys across modules and languages.

localization key get-by-names.summary: Look up localization keys by name.

localization key get.summary: Read one localization key by itemId.

localization key delete-keys.summary: Delete several localization keys in one call.

localization key get-timeline.summary: Read the change history for a localization entity.

localization key get-localization-timeli.summary: Read the tenant-wide localization change history.

localization key get-timeline-by-operati.summary: Read the change history for one async operation.

localization key get-uilm-file.summary: Read a generated UILM language file for a module and language.

localization key generate-uilm-file.summary: Generate a UILM language file for a module.

localization key translate-all.summary: Trigger AI machine translation for every untranslated key in a module.

localization key translate-key.summary: Trigger AI machine translation for one key.

localization key translate-keys.summary: Trigger AI machine translation for several keys.

localization key translate-and-export.details: Without --wait, fires all 3 back to back (same as running them by hand). With --wait, polls GetTimelineByOperationId (using a generated messageCoRelationId) between translate and generate, since translation runs async and there's no documented explicit "done" field to check -- it stops once the timeline entry count settles across 2 polls, or times out with a clear next-step message. Prints one output block per step, not a single combined document.

localization key uilm-import.summary: Import a previously exported UILM file by file id.

localization key uilm-export.summary: Export translation keys as a downloadable UILM file.
localization key uilm-export.details: --output-type selects the format: 0 Json (default), 1 Xml, 2 Text, 3 Xlsx, 4 Csv, 5 Xlf.

localization key get-language-file-gener.summary: List past UILM language-file generation runs.

localization key rollback.summary: Roll back one localization timeline entry.

localization language save.summary: Add or update a language in the tenant's catalog.

localization language list.summary: List languages in the tenant's catalog.

localization language list-for-tenant.summary: List languages enabled for the current tenant.

localization language delete.summary: Remove a language from the tenant's catalog.

localization module save.summary: Create or update a localization module.

localization module list-for-tenant.summary: List localization modules for the current tenant.

localization module tag-glossary.summary: Attach glossary terms to a localization module.

release deploy.summary: Deploy the selected project's environment (Build/manual), optionally syncing secrets and setting the domain first.
release deploy.details: Resolves the repo from --repo (name or id via Build/repos-list) or, when omitted, from the project's linked assets (Project/GetAsset) and that repo's connected branch (Build/repo-details). Aborts if the connected branch doesn't match this environment's name. --with-secrets <dotenvFile> first runs release secrets sync for that file and folds its summary into the final document as secretsSync; --domain also sets the custom deployment domain before deploying. --wait polls the build's status FIELD until a server terminal value (Succeeded/Failed/Cancelled/...; or --timeout elapses, default 900s); --follow implies --wait and streams build events to stderr. All progress goes to stderr, so --json stdout stays one parseable verdict document ({buildId, status, verdict, build}). Mutating; no artifact upload is performed by this CLI.

release setup.summary: First-time deploy of a registered repo (Build/run-build): creates the deployment namespace and push webhook.
release setup.details: Replaces the portal's Configure Deployment modal. Resolves the repo by name or id (auto-picked when only one is registered) and --hosting-provider/--region/--machine-config by name or id against Build/settings; all three are optional (server defaults apply). Refuses when the repo's linked branch doesn't match this project's environment. --wait/--follow behave as in release deploy. Re-deploys of an already-configured repo belong to 'release deploy'. Mutating.

release status.summary: Read one build's status plus a stable verdict (succeeded/failed/running) derived from the status field.
release status.details: Output is {buildId, status, verdict, build}. --wait polls the status field until a server terminal value (progress on stderr); --follow implies --wait and also streams build events to stderr. Read-only.

release logs.summary: Print a build's stored pipeline events (Clone/Build/Deploy/Sast/Sca stages).
release logs.details: Events come from GET Build (no extra endpoint). --group filters to one stage. --follow keeps polling and streaming new events until the build's status field is terminal; in --json mode streamed lines go to stderr and stdout ends with one {buildId, events, status, verdict} document. Read-only.

release builds list.summary: Paged builds of one repository, addressed by name or id.
release builds list.details: Resolves the repo from Build/repos-list: explicit name or id wins, else the single registered repo; multiple repos with no selector fail with repo_ambiguous listing the candidates (never an interactive prompt). --branch filters, --page (1-based) and --page-size (default 30) page through Build/repo-details, and totalCount travels with each page. Read-only.

release repos list.summary: List the repositories registered in blocks-release for the selected project.
release repos list.details: Compact mapped rows: repoId, name, branch, deploymentType, lastDeploymentStatus, lastDeploymentDate, url (custom over default), namespace, repoUrl. Read-only.

release repo get.summary: One registered repo's details plus its most recent builds, addressed by name or id.
release repo get.details: Output is {repo, recentBuilds (up to 5), totalBuilds}. Read-only.

release settings list.summary: Hosting providers, regions, and machine configs valid for 'release setup'.
release settings list.details: Mapped from Build/settings: providers with nested regions and machineConfigs (ids plus names/specs), so setup flags can be chosen in one read. Read-only.

release domain set.summary: Set a repo's custom deployment domain (Build/repo-update).
release domain set.details: Resolves the repo from --repo (name or id) or the single registered repo. Uses the project's environment as projectEnv. Mutating.

release git repos.summary: Browse repositories of the connected source-control account.
release git repos.details: --provider names the VCS and defaults to github -- the only provider active in blocks-release today; anything else fails with provider_not_supported (no rename needed when more providers go live). --search filters; --page (1-based) and --page-size (default 30) page. Requires the GitHub account to be connected from the Blocks portal. Read-only.

release git branches.summary: List branches of one source repository of the connected account.
release git branches.details: --provider defaults to github, the only active provider. Read-only.

release secrets sync.summary: Bulk env-var upsert into a repo's secret set from a dotenv file.
release secrets sync.details: The server stores ONE whole secret set per repo (RepoSecret/save replaces the set), so merge mode reads the current set first -- an audited read, same as the portal's reveal -- and merges the file over it; nothing is ever removed without --prune, which makes the file the entire set and lists the removed key names in the plan. Only the server's not-found answer (no set yet) starts from empty; any other read failure aborts with secrets_read_failed before saving, so a transient error can never wipe the set. --file defaults to .env; --repo/--repo-id picks the repo (auto when only one is registered). Output and --dry-run show key NAMES and counts only -- values are never displayed. A no-change run reports upToDate without calling save. Mutating.

release secrets list.details: Metadata only -- the server never returns key names or values on this endpoint. Read-only.

release secrets lock.summary: Lock a repo's secret set against changes.
release secrets lock.details: Resolves the repo from --repo/--repo-id or the single registered repo. Mutating.

release secrets unlock.details: Resolves the repo from --repo/--repo-id or the single registered repo. Mutating.

release secrets delete.summary: Soft-delete a repo's WHOLE secret set (recoverable with release secrets restore).
release secrets delete.details: The vault value is retained server-side, so restore undoes this. Mutating.

release secrets restore.summary: Restore a repo's soft-deleted secret set.

release secrets audit.summary: Audit trail of a repo's secret set (saves, locks, audited value reads).

release reports get.summary: Security scan report for one build: SAST (SonarQube), SCA (Dependency-Track), or DAST.
release reports get.details: --type is required and must be one of the server's report types: sast (SonarQube), sca-container (Dependency-Track, container image), sca-libraries (Dependency-Track, library manifests), or dast. Anything else fails with invalid_report_type before any request. Read-only.

release monitor list.summary: Monitoring/alerting entries for one deployed repo.
release monitor list.details: Resolves the repo from --repo/--repo-id or the single registered repo. Read-only.

release teardown.summary: DELETE a repo's live deployment: cancels in-flight builds and deletes the Kubernetes namespace.
release teardown.details: Destructive and not undoable, so the repo must be named EXPLICITLY (name or id) -- there is deliberately no fall-back to 'the only repo'. The confirmation states the namespace and served URL being destroyed; --dry-run prints the target first. Mutating.

new web.summary: Create a Vite React starter app that talks to Blocks exclusively through @seliseblocks/client (a single createBlocksClient() instance) using the...
new web.details: Create a Vite React starter app that talks to Blocks exclusively through @seliseblocks/client (a single createBlocksClient() instance) using the SDK hosted IdP flow: blocksClient.auth.idp.redirectToProvider() on login click and blocksClient.auth.idp.callback() on /login/callback. Includes route guards, auto-refresh through auth.oidc.refreshToken(), live auth/iam/localization SDK examples, a Profile landing page, environment config, and safe .gitignore defaults. Uses the selected project (see 'use') unless --x-blocks-key overrides it. --app-domain and --client-id are resolved from the project when omitted: if the project has one domain it's used automatically, otherwise you're prompted to choose; the OIDC client is picked from a list of the project's existing clients, or you can create a minimal one (display name + redirect URI, active, registered as a Blocks OIDC identity provider) on the spot, or skip and register one later from the portal or 'auth oidc-clients save'. Non-interactive callers must provide --app-domain and --client-id or receive interactive_input_required. When a client id resolves, the command checks AuthController and may enable OIDC login. In non-interactive runs, pass --yes only after approving that possible tenant mutation; failure stops before scaffold files are written. If --blocks-api-url is omitted, it is derived from the app domain: https://blocksapi.<registrable-domain> (for example, app domain https://dqrsf.slsblx.com uses https://blocksapi.slsblx.com). Pass a different Data/IAM/Localization/OS gateway URL explicitly only if your project uses a non-default one. --oidc-url defaults to https://iam.seliseblocks.com.
